title: Annotation Reconciliation and Provenance Manifest
author: Priya Khatri
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines the standard process, tooling patterns, metrics and ownership for annotation reconciliation and provenance tracking used by Redwood Inference evaluation pipelines. It is intended for evaluator leads, data engineers, annotation vendors, and product owners that rely on labeled probe sets and human judgments for production quality gates.

Goals:
- Ensure label correctness, reproducibility and auditable lineage for any eval artifact that influences model promotion or rollback decisions.
- Minimize annotation drift and reduce labelling-induced regressions by defining concrete reconciliation steps, thresholds and rollback procedures.
- Provide a lightweight provenance schema that is compatible with our eval-harness ingestion and downstream dashboards.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: probe labeling tasks (classification, intent, slot, response-ranking), canonical ground-truth creation, and post-hoc adjudication for failed probes.
- Not covered: purely synthetic probe generation without human labels, low-risk exploratory annotations for research prototypes.

Ownership and roles

- Annotation Owner (AO): owns the labeling schema, sample packs, and the reconciliation plan. Typically the product or evaluation lead.
- Data Custodian (DC): owns storage of raw annotation artifacts, access control and retention. Typically Data Platform.
- Reconciliation Lead (RL): runs the triangulation workflow and signs-off final label sets.
- Audit Reviewer (AR): independent reviewer (cross-team) who spot-checks provenance and signs compliance for releases that affect customer SLOs.

Minimum metadata and provenance manifest

Every labeled dataset that enters the eval-harness must be accompanied by a flat provenance manifest (JSONL or CSV fields). The eval pipeline expects the following columns (table shown as text):

| field | description | required | example |
|---|---|---:|---|
| dataset_id | internal id used by eval-harness | yes | probe-pack-2026-02-14 |
| schema_version | label schema semantic version | yes | v1.2 |
| source_uri | S3 or GCS path to raw annotations | yes | s3://redwood-evals/probes/pack-2026/annotations.jsonl |
| created_by | annotator id or vendor tag | yes | vendorA_batch_42 |
| created_at | ISO timestamp | yes | 2026-02-10T15:03:00Z |
| reconciliation_run_id | reconciliation job id (if applicable) | conditional | recon-2026-02-12-07 |
| reconciled_by | person or automation that finalized labels | conditional | recon-bot OR Priya Khatri |
| reconciliation_notes | short rationale for changes | conditional | merged label conflicts: majority 3/5; kept gold anchors |
| audit_checks_passed | boolean string (true/false) | yes | true |
| retention_policy | storage TTL label | yes | 2y |

Note: The manifest must be stored alongside the dataset (same bucket/prefix) and registered in the eval-harness catalog via the dataset_id.

Reconciliation workflow (step-by-step)

1) Pre-flight (AO)
   - Freeze schema_version and publish labeling instructions. All changes require a patch note and version bump.
   - Generate anchor set (gold items) of 50–200 probes covering high-risk slices. Anchors carry a single-source-of-truth label created by Subject Matter Experts (SMEs).

2) Labeling (vendor or internal annotators)
   - Collect 3 independent labels per non-anchor probe by default (configurable by task complexity).
   - Emit raw annotations as JSONL with fields: probe_id, annotator_id, label, confidence, payload.

3) Automated conflict detection (DC)
   - Run a conflict detection job that computes inter-annotator agreement (IAA) per-slice and flags probes where majority agreement < 0.6 or where label entropy > threshold (default 0.8).
   - Produce conflicts CSV at s3://redwood-evals/{dataset_id}/conflicts.csv

4) Triaging conflicts (RL)
   - Resolve conflicts via the following ordered strategies until resolved:
     a) Majority rule if agreement >= 0.5 and no anchor disagreement.
     b) SME adjudication for anchors and high-severity slices (see severity mapping below).
     c) Pairwise adjudication: present annotator pair histories and ask RL to pick or suggest a new label (allow relabeling across categories).
     d) Consensus adjudication meeting for ambiguous probe families (calendar scheduled within 48 hours).

5) Finalization and provenance capture (RL + DC)
   - Produce reconciled JSONL with final_label, rationale_tag, reconciled_at, reconciled_by.
   - Update the provenance manifest (reconciliation_run_id and reconciliation_notes).
   - Push reconciled artifact to a guarded prefix (e.g., /reconciled/) and set read-only ACLs.

6) Audit and sign-off (AR)
   - AR must sample at least 5% of reconciled probes or 200 items (whichever is larger) across slices and verify: manifest correctness, frozen schema_version, anchor agreement intact.
   - AR signs off by updating 'audit_checks_passed' to true in manifest and adding a short audit log entry.

Severity mapping and when to require SME adjudication

- Severity: high/medium/low (example mapping)
  - High: probes that directly affect customer-facing decision logic or safety sentinels (anchor mismatch -> SME required).
  - Medium: slices with business impact but not immediate safety effect (default RL adjudication allowed).
  - Low: exploratory labels or internal-only slices (automated reconciliation acceptable).

Inter-annotator agreement (IAA) and thresholds

- Global acceptance criteria for production ground-truth:
  - Krippendorff's alpha >= 0.65 OR majority agreement >= 0.7 across core slices.
  - For high-severity slices, alpha >= 0.75 and anchors must remain unchanged.
- If thresholds are not met for any critical slice, labeling batch must be escalated to SME review and reannotation plan.

Automated checks and sample SQL snippets

- Conflict count per probe (Postgres example):
  SELECT probe_id, COUNT(DISTINCT annotator_id) as n, COUNT(DISTINCT label) as label_count
  FROM eval_annotations
  WHERE dataset_id = 'probe-pack-2026-02-14'
  GROUP BY probe_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT label) > 1;

- Slice-level entropy (BigQuery):
  SELECT slice_name, SUM(-p * LOG(p)) as entropy
  FROM ( SELECT slice_name, label, COUNT(1) / SUM(COUNT(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY slice_name) as p
         FROM `project.dataset.annotations`
         WHERE dataset_id='probe-pack-2026-02-14'
         GROUP BY slice_name, label )
  GROUP BY slice_name
  ORDER BY entropy DESC;

- Quick conflict resolver (Python sketch):
  import json, collections
  def consolidate(annotations):
      counts = collections.Counter(a['label'] for a in annotations)
      label, count = counts.most_common(1)[0]
      if count >= 2:
          return label, 'majority'
      return None, 'conflict'

Quality gates and SLOs for annotation processes

- Turnaround SLAs:
  - Automated conflict detection: within 2 hours of raw ingestion.
  - Reconciliation initial triage: within 48 hours of conflict detection.
  - Full SME adjudication: within 5 business days for high-severity items.

- Quality SLOs (monthly rolling):
  - Anchors agreement retention: 99.5% remain unchanged unless schema_version bump.
  - Reconciliation precision: sample-verified precision >= 95% (AR sampling).
  - Dataset completeness: 100% manifest fields populated.

Versioning and schema evolution

- SemVer-style schema_version managed in the repo: schemas/label-schemas.yaml. Changes must include: change log, migration plan, sample migration script.
- Backwards compatibility rule: readers must be tolerant of older schema fields; conversions should be defined in data-platform transformations.

Retention and access controls

- Default retention: 2 years for reconciled artifacts, 90 days for raw transient annotations (unless flagged for legal retention).
- Access: Reconciled artifacts are read-only to non-DC teams. DC and AO have write privileges. Export for external vendors require signed NDA and temporary access tokens.

Integration with eval-harness and pipelines

- Registration: After reconciliation, AO must register the dataset_id in the eval-harness catalog using the CLI:
  redwood-evalctl register --dataset-id probe-pack-2026-02-14 --manifest-uri s3://redwood-evals/probes/pack-2026/manifest.jsonl --schema v1.2
\- The pipeline will reject dataset registrations missing required manifest fields.

Failure modes and remediation

- Failure: Anchors drift after reconciliation. Remediation: freeze rollouts, notify model-ops and product, re-run anchor validation and if >2% anchor divergence, rollback promotions that used the dataset.
- Failure: IAA below threshold across many slices. Remediation: escalate to SME, possibly re-run labeling with expanded annotator training and updated instructions.

Operational runbook (short)

- If conflict CSV shows >5% probes in conflict:
  1) RL opens triage ticket in JIRA with dataset_id and attaches conflicts.csv.
  2) AO schedules SME review within 48 hours.
  3) DC marks dataset status as 'recon-in-progress' in catalog.
  4) After reconciliation, publish reconciled artifact and update manifest.

Examples and sample artifacts

- Sample manifest JSONL line:
  {"dataset_id":"probe-pack-2026-02-14","schema_version":"v1.2","source_uri":"s3://redwood-evals/probes/pack-2026/annotations.jsonl","created_by":"vendorA_batch_42","created_at":"2026-02-10T15:03:00Z","reconciliation_run_id":"recon-2026-02-12-07","reconciled_by":"Priya Khatri","reconciliation_notes":"majority-resolved; anchors validated","audit_checks_passed":"true","retention_policy":"2y"}

- Label file snippet (JSONL):
  {"probe_id":"p-0001","annotator_id":"ann_01","label":"billing_issue","confidence":0.9}
  {"probe_id":"p-0001","annotator_id":"ann_07","label":"billing_issue","confidence":0.8}
  {"probe_id":"p-0001","annotator_id":"ann_12","label":"account_problem","confidence":0.6}

Open decisions and future improvements

- Decide whether to adopt probabilistic label fusion (Bayesian aggregation) for low-consensus slices — pilot proposed Q2 2026.
- Evaluate integrating per-annotator reliability scores into reconciliation logic to reduce SME load.

Appendix: checklist for dataset publish (to paste into PR)

- [ ] schema_version bumped and documented
- [ ] provenance manifest present and complete
- [ ] anchor set verified and unchanged (or documented if changed)
- [ ] conflict CSV reviewed and reconciled
- [ ] AR sampling passed and log recorded
- [ ] retention and ACLs set correctly
